title: Galactic Encounters
subtitle: Galaxies grow by meeting
description: Interactive walk through tidal forces, tails and bridges, stars versus gas, Antennae, Whirlpool, Mice, major versus minor mergers, remnants, and the uncertain Milky Way–Andromeda future.
source_note: Encounter labs ILLUSTRATIVE. Observed systems use ESA/Hubble media. MW–M31 section is FUTURE PREDICTION / SIMULATION and model-dependent.

steps.title: Galaxies are not islands
steps.narration_text: Galaxies influence one another across millions of light-years. This walk separates observation, simulation, illustration, and future prediction.

steps.title: Gravity across millions of light-years
steps.narration_text: Gravity is the main handshake. Dark-matter halos dominate the mass and steer long orbits between galaxies.

steps.title: First passage
steps.narration_text: Advance the encounter lab from approach through first passage. A flyby does not finish a merger overnight—timescales are hundreds of millions to billions of years.

steps.title: Tidal tails and bridges
steps.narration_text: Differential gravity stretches disks: the near side feels a stronger pull than the far side. Tails and bridges are the long signatures of that stretch.

steps.title: Stars mostly miss
steps.narration_text: When galaxies overlap, stars almost never smash into each other. Stellar separations dwarf stellar sizes.

steps.title: Gas collides
steps.narration_text: Gas clouds can compress and shock, helping light new stars. Not every encounter makes the same starburst.

steps.title: The Antennae
steps.narration_text: NGC 4038 and 4039 are a classic merger with long tidal antennae and intense star formation. Hubble imaging is an observation; the lab remains illustrative.

steps.title: The Whirlpool
steps.narration_text: M51 and its companion show how interactions can help organize spiral structure while the pair continues to dance.

steps.title: The Mice
steps.narration_text: NGC 4676 flaunts twin tidal tails—visual proof of strong tidal stripping during an encounter.

steps.title: Major vs minor mergers
steps.narration_text: Major mergers scramble peers of similar mass. Minor mergers let large galaxies grow by absorbing smaller ones, often leaving streams or shells.

steps.title: What remains
steps.narration_text: Remnants are diverse: disturbed disks, elliptical-like shapes, rebuilt gas-rich disks, starbursts, or AGN if fuel reaches the central black hole. Visit Black Holes for horizon-scale physics.

steps.title: Milky Way meets Andromeda?
steps.narration_text: Andromeda approaches on billion-year timescales. Label this FUTURE PREDICTION slash SIMULATION: exact timing and geometry remain model-dependent.

steps.title: Galaxies grow by encounter
steps.narration_text: From Antennae tails to our own Local Group future, encounters write galaxy history. Exit and Restore returns Stellarium when you are done.
